title: prefill/decode pipeline: chunked prefill, speculative prefill, and stage overlap
author: Diego Ramirez
description: Motivation: reduce end-to-end tail latency and improve GPU utilization for mixed prefill/decode workloads by letting prefill and decode stages overlap, and by making prefill streaming chunked and speculative to warm KV cache earlier. This PR implements three coordinated changes: (1) chunked prefill iterator so long prefill sequences are sent in smaller micro-batches to the runtime, reducing head-of-line blocking; (2) speculative prefill scheduling that starts prefill KV population earlier for likely continuation tokens using a lightweight predictor, and cancels speculative work when not needed; (3) StageOverlap executor in the serving runtime that schedules prefill, KV materialization, and decode on separate worker pools with controlled handoff to enable overlap while preserving deterministic ordering where required. Results: in our perf lab with mix-ratio workloads (50% short decode-only, 50% long prefill+decode) we see median P95 end-to-end latency improvement of ~18-24% and tail (P99) reductions up to 30% on A100p4 instances. GPU utilization improved by ~12% while average tokens/sec increased by 9%. Changes are behind an opt-in runtime flag (runtime.enable_stage_overlap) and conservative defaults for canary rollout. Checklist: Implement chunked prefill iterator and API, Add speculative scheduler + config knobs, Add StageOverlap executor and metrics, Unit + integration tests, Perf harness and benchmarks, Docs + changelog. Related: builds on learnings from pr-21456-prefill-decode-pipeline-optimizations and tracks Linear items ENG-1723 and ENG-1840. Notes: speculative prefill is safe-by-default (limits speculative occupancy and cost accounting), KV cache is updated atomically to avoid partial visibility, and a fallback path reverts to previous pipeline when the feature flag is off.

review_conversation: Maya Chen: Can you clarify how ordering guarantees are preserved when overlapping prefill and decode?

Author (Diego): The StageOverlap executor preserves logical ordering by tagging requests with sequence tokens. Hand-off includes a fence that ensures prefill KV publishes are visible before dependent decodes proceed. Added tests to validate ordering under heavy concurrency.
Oliver Grant: Speculative prefill looks useful but could increase cost. How are speculative entries accounted for?

Author (Diego): Speculative work is limited by a per-request budget and global speculative concurrency cap. Speculative KV entries are tagged and evicted preferentially; billing attribution uses a gate that attributes tokens only when speculative results are materialized for a real request. Added metrics to monitor speculative hit/miss and cost impact.
Priya Singh: Any perf regressions on short-context-only workloads?

Author (Diego): We ran short-context benchmarks; with the feature disabled there is zero change. With feature enabled and defaults we see neutral to slightly better latency due to reduced head-of-line blocking. We include guardrails to disable overlap when workload is decode-only heavy.
